correctness.rationale: Every numerical semigroup has the unique parent obtained by adjoining its Frobenius gap; children are generated by deletion of eligible minimal generators greater than parent Frobenius, so the rooted tree exhausts all S by genus without overlap. Inspected C++ implementation enumerates all nodes to g=27 and tests only nonsymmetric parents via exact generator products and residue Dijkstra Apéry sets of S^<2>, with g=(sum w)/m^2-(m^2-1)/2 and F=max(w)-m^2. The finite 128-bit encoding safely contains gaps because F<=2g-1<=53. Two split run logs cover g0..24 and g25..27 and match standard genus counts, totaling 3,220,696. An independent rewritten C++ enumeration agrees through its completed generations, while upper-genus replay completion is not asserted. This proves an explicit finite cutoff only, not the unknown exact minimal genus.

This is substantive finite mathematical data, not a tiny arbitrary instance or a claim to solve the unknown exact minimum.
